description:
A linked checkout created by the test itself proves refusal, stance-based permission, and
the override audit record from the boundary an adopter invokes.

## Background

The reported field incident began in a linked worker checkout whose mutations silently built
a divergent store. An existing integration suite already creates real linked checkouts with
version-control commands, and it is the target with the most room for new modules under the
repository's test-target budget, so this coverage lands there rather than claiming a scarce
target slot.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: Under the refusing stance, a state-mutating invocation inside a test-created linked checkout is rejected and leaves that checkout's store and event log unchanged.
- [hard] REQ-02: The same invocation succeeds under a permitting declared stance and emits no override record, and succeeds under an explicit per-invocation override leaving the durable override record behind.
- [hard] REQ-03: The refusal observed at this boundary carries the machine-readable facts the policy promises: the linked checkout, the refusing stance, and how to permit the operation.
- [hard] REQ-04: The coverage lands as modules of an existing test target and keeps the suite inside the repository's measured budgets.
title: Linked-checkout write-policy journey
